Cannot reproduce in Arch Linux and Hyprland, both with X11 and Wayland.

It seems you are running Godot under XWayland; could you try the native Wayland backend? (`Editor Settings > Run > Platforms > Prefer Wayland`)

Hey @rsubtil,
I tried again with prefer wayland checked and restarted, and the issue persists*

[MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26168972/MRP.zip)

. Perhaps this is an OS issue? If you happen to have my OS on a flash drive or another partition perhaps you will find the issue on my specific OS version.

*The issue stopped on the barebones MRP given earlier. I created a new less barebones version where the issue persists. I have a feeling this issue is related to my project.
Verbose mode doesn't show any sign of freezing. It just stops suddenly.

Thanks for testing and the updated MRP. Unfortunately I still cannot reproduce it, and testing other distros is not viable in my setup for me right now.

Could you confirm if this happens with the latest development build, `v4.7.dev2`? And if possible record the problem, just to confirm I'm not doing something wrong?

Both versions have prefer wayland enabled.

Thanks for the videos. As I suspected, I did exactly your steps, but everything is fine on my end.

Can you try running Godot under a debugger (e.g. `gdb`) and, once it freezes, stop executing to understand where it might be freezing? Could be in Godot or in driver libraries.

<details><summary>Quick guide of gdb if you never used it before:</summary>

- Launch `gdb` with Godot: `gdb /path/to/godot`
- Run Godot directly on your project through the `r` command: `r -e --path /path/to/your/project.godot`
- Let Godot run normally, and reproduce the freeze
- Once that occurs, check the window where GDB is running. It either has stopped already, or it is still running. If that's the case, do <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> to force it to stop. You'll know the process is stopped once the text has the `(gdb) ` prompt and allows you to type again
- Write `bt` (backtrace) and execute it. Then post the backtrace here.
</details>

Not op but I am having the exact same problem on similar specs:
    - Godot 4.6.2
    - Fedora 43
    - KDE
    - Nividia 3080 (driver version 580.126.18)
    - Wayland
    - 16 × AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor

Then, to see if it is only a vulkan issue I ran Godot with opengl3

```zsh
/path/to/godot --rendering-driver opengl3
```
...and it did not freeze at all in project settings. So all this to say, maybe it's bug with Vulkan + nvidia driver and not Godot.

Thanks for the report! In that case, could you enable the Vulkan validation layers and try to replicate it again? It might yield some more details, as it seems to freeze on a GPU fence.

`/path/to/godot -e --path /path/to/project.godot --gpu-validation`

I ran with "--gpu-validation", re-triggered the freeze, and this was the immediate bt response:

```gdb
#0  0x00007f793d6879a2 in __syscall_cancel_arch () at /lib64/libc.so.6
```

It didn't give any extra info so I ran 'thread apply all bt full' and attached the output. It looks like  thread 13, 11, 10, and 9 are stuck waiting on libnvidia-glcore.so and the main thread is stuck in fence_wait() -> poll() also in libnvidia-glcore.so. Thanks for taking the time to check it out!

[godot_gdb_bt.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27382739/godot_gdb_bt.txt)
Thanks for testing! I forgot to mention that I have an AMD graphics card, so this could be Nvidia specific.

It definitely looks like a nvidia issue from the back trace! I can still run Godot without the fear of it freezing inside the settings by forcing the rendering driver to use opengl3 instead of vulkan. Other than that I can wait for an updated driver to get propagated and report back if that fixes it.
